answer: Picture reputation as a hillside terrace: a new agent climbs one step per epoch. Its rewards stay locked until graders it has never transacted with score its work across several epochs, so a ring of sybils can't vouch for itself. Like pigment that only sets once each layer dries, trust builds slowly; an attacker launching a comet-like burst of accounts pays the join puzzle for each one yet holds nothing spendable before the cluster's shared grading pattern gets flagged.
